name: Signal Writes Claim An Idle Change Queue

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Signal Writes Claim An Idle Change Queue Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

An observed `Signal::set`/`replace`/`update` pushes its change under the signal lock and drains afterwards: three change-queue round trips (push, claim and pop, empty check). Claiming an idle queue in the push's critical section (experiment 38's `push_or_claim`) and delivering the change after the signal lock is released saves one, with the same commit-order delivery. Deferred writers used by `Computed` keep pushing.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** push-or-claim for the immediate signal writers.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/signal.rs` (commit helpers and `set`/`replace`/`update`), a crate-visible re-export of `ClaimedDrain` in `crates/src/primitives/mod.rs`.
**Forbidden in this experiment:** deferred writers, Computed, values() startup, DeliveryQueue internals.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Scalar tests and full lib + integration + doc-example tests; clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` scalar-hot and `reactive_complexity` vs base, rerun borderline. Pass: signal-set-one-subscriber or effect-on-filtered-map >=8% faster; nothing slower >10% on rerun.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

~3-5 ns less per observed signal write.

**Passed Status**: false — Reverted failure.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** all tests pass, but effect-on-filtered-map regressed to 42-50 ns in three runs while a control run of the unchanged checkpoint measured 23 ns; computed chain +7% in three runs; signal-set-one-subscriber was bimodal (21/49/80 ns vs 22.7 ns control). The claimed path is slower than push+drain for signal writes.
**Out-of-scope changes:** none.
